name: Intra-Corporate Transfer (ICT) permit

requirements.blocker_text: This requires at least 3 months' prior employment with the same corporate group before the transfer.
This requires transferring as a manager, specialist, or trainee employee.
This requires a market-conform salary — IND benchmarks this against the Highly Skilled Migrant thresholds rather than publishing a separate statutory figure.

evidence_required.document: Assignment letter confirming intra-group transfer terms and duration
Proof of 3+ months' prior employment within the group

outcome.duration_length: up to 3 years (managers/specialists), up to 1 year (trainees), cannot be extended beyond that

notes: Directly comparable to Germany's de_ict_card and structurally similar in outcome — deliberately terminal (leads_to_pr false, switchable_to empty, not renewable beyond the cap), since this implements the same EU ICT Directive (2014/66/EU) as Germany's version, just via a different national implementing statute. Prior-employment requirement is shorter here (3 months) than Germany's (6 months) — a genuine, confirmed cross-country difference worth surfacing in a comparison view. 6-month cooling-off before a new ICT permit, same as Germany. EU short-term mobility (up to 90 days in other member states by notification) and long-term mobility to other Directive-adopting states (not Denmark/Ireland) apply, same pattern as the German route.
